# function: render_device_configs

Processes a Network as Code model structure to produce fully rendered per-device configurations. Handles template evaluation, deep merging with precedence cascade (global → group → template instance → device), interface group merging, and CLI template collection. Supports nxos, iosxe, and iosxr architectures. Returns an error if the same attribute is a different kind of value (map, list, or scalar) at different precedence levels; scalar values and types may otherwise differ across levels, with the more specific level taking precedence.

The `raw` output keeps `!env` tags unresolved, also where variables with `!env` tags are used in templates, while the `resolved` output resolves them, so that variables with `!env` tags can be used within strings (e.g. `Bearer ${token}`). In the `raw` output, a value consisting only of an `!env` tag is kept as `!env VAR` and written as a YAML tag by `yaml_encode`, so that YAML loaders with `!env` support (e.g. `nac-validate`, `nac-test`) resolve it. A tag used within a string is kept as text (e.g. `Bearer !env TOKEN`), which these tools do not resolve. If such a value needs to be resolved there, use a tag for the whole value instead (e.g. an environment variable containing `Bearer ...`).

The names in the `templates` lists of `global`, the device groups and the devices must be templates of type `file`, `model` or `cli`; unknown templates and templates of other types are reported as errors, all at once.

CLI templates are named after their template: `<template>` for templates of `global` and the device, `<template>/<group>` for device group templates and `<template>/instance/<instance>` for template instances. An entry replaces an earlier entry with the same name, in increasing order of precedence (`global`, device groups, template instances, device templates, then the device's `cli_templates`), e.g. a template assigned both to `global` and to the device is only rendered once, and a device's `cli_templates` entry replaces a template of the same name.

~> This function is intended for use within the [Network as Code](https://netascode.cisco.com/) Terraform modules and is not intended for standalone use.

## Template Variables

The following variables are available inside `${}` template expressions in model templates, file templates, CLI templates, configuration values and interface group configurations:

- The `variables` of `global`, the device groups the device belongs to and the device, in increasing order of precedence. Templates of a device group additionally see that group's own `variables` on top of the device variables.
- `GLOBAL`: the whole architecture section of the merged model (e.g. `GLOBAL.devices`).
- `DEVICES`: all devices of the model in model order, including devices not managed in this run, each with its `name`, the names of the `device_groups` it belongs to (devices listing the group and devices listed by the group, in device group order, followed by groups the device lists that are not defined), the names of the `template_instances` targeting it (by `devices` or `device_groups`, in instance order, also if all items of an instance are narrowed to other devices) and its `variables` (the variables of `global`, its device groups and the device, merged as for the device's own templates). This allows templates to refer to other devices, e.g. `[for d in DEVICES : d.variables.mgmt_ip if contains(d.device_groups, "VPC") && d.name != DEVICE.name]`.
- `DEVICE`: the device being rendered, i.e. its element of `DEVICES` (e.g. `DEVICE.name`, `contains(DEVICE.device_groups, "LEAFS")`, `contains(DEVICE.template_instances, "SERVICE_PROD_WEB")`, `DEVICE.variables.leaf_id`). This allows a single template attached to a device group or `global` to select the entries of a shared list that apply to the device, e.g. `%{ for e in endpoints ~}%{ if contains(e.switches, DEVICE.name) ~}...%{ endif ~}%{ endfor ~}` in a file template.

A user variable named `GLOBAL`, `DEVICES` or `DEVICE` takes precedence over the built-in variable of the same name.

## Template Instances

A template instance (`<arch>.template_instances`) applies a template to a set of devices with its own variables, e.g. one instance per service, without a device group per service:

- `name` (required, unique, without `/`) identifies the instance in error messages and in the names of CLI templates (`<template>/instance/<instance>`, which differ from the names of device group CLI templates, `<template>/<group>`, also if a device group has the same name).
- `template` (required) is the name of a `file`, `model` or `cli` template in `<arch>.templates`.
- `devices` and `device_groups` select the devices the instance applies to (at least one is required). Device groups include devices listing the group and devices listed by the group.
- `variables` are only visible to this instance. Its template sees the variables of `global`, the device groups and the device (as other templates do), then the instance `variables`, in increasing order of precedence, plus `GLOBAL`, `DEVICES` and `DEVICE`.
- `items` renders the template once per item, each with its own `variables` on top of the instance `variables`. An instance without `items` (or with `items` set to null) renders the template once, `items: []` not at all. An item's `devices` and `device_groups` narrow the devices of the instance: devices must be devices of the instance, device groups select the devices of the instance that are members. An item's optional `name` (unique within the instance, without `/`) names its CLI templates `<template>/instance/<instance>/<name>`, which do not change when items are added or reordered; CLI templates of items without a name are named `<template>/instance/<instance>/items[<index>]`.

Unknown attributes, templates, devices and device groups, values of the wrong type, duplicate names and devices of an item outside its instance are reported as errors, all at once. The configurations of template instances are merged after the device group configurations and before the device templates, in instance and item order. Template instances (or items of one instance) setting a value in a map to different values on a device are reported as errors; equal values (e.g. a feature enabled by several instances) are allowed. List items are merged by their values, so instances adding the same list item (e.g. a VLAN ID) with different values result in two list items, which fails when the configuration is applied (e.g. as a duplicate key in the Terraform module).

## Template Functions

The following functions are available inside `${}` template expressions in model templates, file templates, and CLI templates:

**Numeric:** `abs`, `ceil`, `floor`, `log`, `max`, `min`, `parseint`, `pow`, `signum`, `sum`

**String:** `chomp`, `endswith`, `format`, `formatlist`, `indent`, `join`, `lower`, `regex`, `regexall`, `regexreplace`, `replace`, `sort`, `split`, `startswith`, `strcontains`, `strlen`, `substr`, `title`, `trim`, `trimprefix`, `trimsuffix`, `trimspace`, `upper`

**Collection:** `chunklist`, `coalesce`, `coalescelist`, `compact`, `concat`, `contains`, `distinct`, `element`, `flatten`, `index`, `keys`, `length`, `lookup`, `merge`, `one`, `range`, `reverse`, `setintersection`, `setproduct`, `setsubtract`, `setunion`, `slice`, `values`, `zipmap`

**Type Conversion:** `tobool`, `tonumber`, `tostring`

**Encoding:** `base64decode`, `base64encode`, `csvdecode`, `jsondecode`, `jsonencode`

**IP Network:** `cidrcontains`, `cidrhost`, `cidrnetmask`, `cidrsubnet`, `cidrsubnets` (as in Terraform, except that host and subnet numbers that do not fit the prefix are errors, IPv4-mapped IPv6 prefixes are supported by `cidrhost` and `cidrsubnets` can allocate subnets at the start of the address space; `cidrcontains` as in OpenTofu)

**Date/Time:** `formatdate`, `timeadd`

**Boolean:** `alltrue`, `anytrue`

**Error Handling:** `try`, `can`, `fail`

`fail(message)` stops rendering with the message as error, e.g. `${contains(vlans, vlan) ? vlan : fail("VLAN ${vlan} is not defined")}`. Only the selected branch of a conditional (or `%{ if }` directive) is evaluated, and `try` and `can` catch the error.

**Network:** `parse_vlans`, `expand_interfaces`

`parse_vlans(vlans)` converts VLANs in CLI notation (a number, a string such as `"10,20-29"`, or a list of them) to the `ids` and `ranges` object the device data models use for VLAN lists, e.g. `parse_vlans([10, "20-29"])` returns `{ids = [10], ranges = [{from = 20, to = 29}]}`, for use as `trunk_allowed_vlans: ${jsonencode(parse_vlans(vlans))}` (nxos) or `trunk_allowed_vlans: {vlans: ${jsonencode(parse_vlans(vlans))}}` (iosxe). An empty list returns an empty object and null returns null. Invalid VLANs (other than IDs from 1 to 4094 and ranges of them, e.g. `all`) are reported as errors.

`expand_interfaces(interfaces)` expands interface ranges in CLI notation (a string such as `"1/10,1/20-23"`, or a list of them) to a list of interface IDs, e.g. `["1/10", "1/20", "1/21", "1/22", "1/23"]`, in the given order. A range applies to the last number of an ID (e.g. `1/1/1-4` for breakout ports, `10-12` for port-channels) and covers at most 1024 interfaces.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    utils = {
      source = "netascode/utils"
    }
  }
}

provider "utils" {}

locals {
  model = {
    nxos = {
      templates = [
        {
          name = "base_config"
          type = "model"
          configuration = {
            system = {
              mtu = "$${mtu}"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
      global = {
        templates = ["base_config"]
        variables = {
          mtu = 9216
        }
        configuration = {
          system = {
            dns_server = "10.0.0.53"
          }
        }
      }
      devices = [
        {
          name = "switch1"
          url  = "https://switch1.example.com"
          configuration = {
            system = {
              hostname = "switch1"
            }
          }
        },
        {
          name = "switch2"
          url  = "https://switch2.example.com"
          configuration = {
            system = {
              hostname = "switch2"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }

  result = provider::utils::render_device_configs([], local.model, "", {}, [], [])
}

# Each device has fully rendered configuration and metadata
output "switch1" {
  value = local.result.raw.nxos.devices[0]
}

# Provider devices list for configuring the provider
output "provider_devices" {
  value = local.result.provider_devices
}

/*
switch1 = {
  "cli_templates" = []
  "configuration" = {
    "system" = {
      "dns_server" = "10.0.0.53"
      "hostname"   = "switch1"
      "mtu"        = 9216
    }
  }
  "managed" = true
  "name"    = "switch1"
  "url"     = "https://switch1.example.com"
}
*/
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
render_device_configs(yaml_strings list of string, model dynamic, defaults_yaml string, file_templates dynamic, managed_devices list of string, managed_device_groups list of string) object
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `yaml_strings` (List of String) List of YAML strings to decode and merge into the base model.
1. `model` (Dynamic) HCL model variable to merge on top of the YAML strings.
1. `defaults_yaml` (String) Module defaults YAML string. User defaults from model override these.
1. `file_templates` (Dynamic) Map of file path to pre-read file content for file-type templates.
1. `managed_devices` (List of String) List of device names to manage. Empty list means all devices.
1. `managed_device_groups` (List of String) List of device group names to manage. Empty list means all device groups.
